messages:
Anya: kicked off a small A/B for the summary route — comparing v4p1-int8-batched (batch-size=8, kv-cache warm) vs v4p1-int4-stream (streaming, smaller mem footprint). each at 5% traffic for now.
Sam: nice. can you paste the gating criteria again?
Anya: sure — SLOs we care about: latency P95 <= 250ms, hallucination (extraneous facts) delta <= +1.5% vs control, and token-cost reduction >= 20% for the quantized variant. auto-fallback if any of the first two breach for 3 consecutive 5m buckets.
Jordan: how are we computing hallucination? which eval set?
Anya: using 'summaries_eval_v2' (5k examples, mixed length). metric = rate of hallucination tokens flagged by heuristic + human-sampled adjudication. quick note: streaming variant shows lower cost but slightly higher hallucination in the first smoke run.
Sam: paste smoke outputs? would like to see numbers.
Anya: sure — smoke run (5k samples) results:
```
control (v4p1 fp16): p95=210ms, hall_rate=1.6%, cost_per_k=1.00
int8-batched: p95=225ms, hall_rate=1.9%, cost_per_k=0.78
int4-stream: p95=245ms, hall_rate=2.3%, cost_per_k=0.62
```
Sam: hmm int8-batched meets cost but hall_rate +0.3% vs control — within our +1.5% delta, so fine. int4-stream > +0.7% which is still <1.5% but closer. latency also creeping on int4-stream.
Jordan: any slice mismatches? long-docs vs short-docs?
Anya: yes — split by seqlen:
- short (<200 tokens): int4-stream perf good, hall ~ +0.4%
- medium (200-800): int4-stream hall +0.9%, p95 ~ +40ms
- long (>800): int4-stream hall +1.8%, p95 +80ms (this is the main pain)
Eva: so long-doc slice is the issue — do we have KV warmup differences? maybe stream path not warming cache.
Anya: exactly. KV hit-rate for int4-stream on long-doc slice is 62% vs 89% for batched control. looks like continuous-batching helped warm the cache.
Sam: what's our current plan? progressive ramp or abort?
Anya: proposal: promote int8-batched on a phased 10/25/50 schedule with standard canary checks. keep int4-stream in shadow for now while we tune the KV warmup and rerun. if any 5m bucket shows hall delta >1.5% OR p95 increase >30ms for a slice flagged as high-impact (long-doc) -> immediate rollback and throttle to 0% for that variant.
Jordan: can we implement slice-aware fallback so int4-stream is excluded for long-docs but allowed for short/medium? that would preserve cost wins.
Sam: technially yes — route-level policy can include seqlen tagging. we should ensure the routing signal is reliable.
Eva: +1 to slice-aware policy. also add a rule: if cost wins >25% and overall hall delta < +0.8% we can auto-promote faster (two-step) after second check.
Anya: I'll update the rollout config. also adding a short probe that forces kv-warm path for 200 long-docs to see immediate effect. run id: deploy-1743337777-ab1
deploy-bot: deploy started: variant int8-batched -> 5% (route: /summary) | int4-stream -> 5% (shadow=false) | run_id=deploy-1743337777-ab1
Sam: pinging eval infra to stream real-time metrics to #eng-metrics. can you add an alert for hall_delta > 1.2% for any 5m window on long-doc slice?
Anya: done — alert created (alert-id: hall_delta_long_1743). Also added an automated rollback playbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/rollback-ab
Jordan: action items: (1) Anya tune rollout config with slice exemptions + faster-promote rule; (2) Sam hook alert into run; (3) Eva run kv-warm microprobe and post results; (4) I'll draft a short customer-impact note if we need to rollback.
Anya: I'll push the rollout config in 10m and update this thread with the exact policy blob. :thumbsup:
Eva: started the warmup probe now — running 200 long-doc probes with forced sequential kv priming, will share perf snapshot in ~12m.
Sam: noted. if int8-batched looks stable we'll promote it and save some cost while we fix int4-stream. :money_with_wings:
Anya: thanks everyone — will update with the config + first 15m metrics shortly."
